item.title: 42.2 km of longing: Bereaved family members run in Chicago Marathon
item.description: 25 bereaved family members and fellow runners take part in the Chicago Marathon, running in memory of loved ones. The team left Israel on October 7, three years after the massacre, following months of joint training.

item.description: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich warns that a change of government could threaten yeshivas, religious institutions and Jewish communities in Judea and Samaria.

item.title: Mysterious cave found in central Israel
item.description: Digging tools found in a cave near Rosh HaAyin. The IDF ruled out a tunnel but circumstances surrounding the excavation are still under investigation.

item.title: Suspected terror attack attempt: Palestinian from Al-Eizariya arrested with knife
item.description:
Police officers from the Judea and Samaria District and Border Police forces arrested a Palestinian Arab man in his 20s, a resident of Al-Eizariya, following a report that he had expressed an intention to carry out a terrorist attack imminently.
The suspect, who was masked, was located and arrested in the village of Al-Eizariya while carrying a knife and a glass cup containing nails and paper, which are suspected of having been intended for throwing and setting on fire.
The suspect was transferred for questioning at the Ma'ale Adumim police station and taken into custody.
The investigation is ongoing and is being conducted by the counterterrorism unit of the Judea and Samaria District Central Investigations Unit.

item.description: 300-meter section of ancient aqueduct dating to the Hasmonean period discovered during excavations ahead of construction of new Jerusalem neighborhood. Historic structure to be preserved and displayed to the public.

item.title: Avinatan Or’s mother reveals captor’s final words: 'Hamas is weak'
item.description: Ditza Or says a Hamas captor told her son the group was too weak to hold the remaining hostages, arguing that military pressure forced their release.

item.title: Mystery on the Lebanese border
item.description: IDF radar systems detected an unidentified object in the skies near the Israel-Lebanon border last night. IDF forces are conducting ground and aerial searches in an attempt to determine what it was.

item.title: Arutz Sheva poll: One-third of secular Israelis see plane rescue as ‘divine providence’
item.description: Nearly all Haredi and religious respondents attribute the rescue of passengers on the flight from Dubai to “Divine Providence," as do most traditional Jews.

item.title: Ex-AG Mandelblit to testify in Netanyahu's trial
item.description: Former Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit is set to testify for Netanyahu’s defense, with questioning expected to focus on investigative approvals and alleged pressure.

item.title: The obligation of Torah study for men
item.description: Knowing the Torah’s guidance for living obligates men and women equally. Encompassing the entire Torah, commandments that are relevant to the learner’s life and those that are not, and continued study of the Torah in depth, obligates only men.

item.title: Yoni Levi to Mamdani: 'If you can't tell the difference, you're part of that evil'
item.description: Yonit Levi responds to NYC Mayor's Oct. 7 statements, arguing against comparing the massacre to Israel's war, and saying that doing so on that day in particular is 'inexcusable.'

item.title: Ahead of elections: Likud searches for political defectors
item.description: Likud has established a team of MKs and strategic advisers to examine candidates from Gadi Eisenkot's party, aiming to persuade lawmakers to join the right-wing bloc after the elections.

item.title: France is burning. Europe will fall into darkness
item.description: What is happening in France concerns the entire West. These are extremely serious social-racial uprisings aimed at the destruction of our countries and our culture. Opinion.

item.title: Trump on the Houthi attack on Riyadh: It's terrible
item.description:
In a conversation with reporters, US President Donald Trump referred to the Houthi attack on Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, and condemned it, saying: "I think it's terrible."
When asked whether the United States military would intervene following the attack, Trump replied curtly: "You'll find out."
